SolutionEditor.help: A rich-text editor where the student writes their own solution; the tutor responds to what they wrote (never the full answer).
SolutionEditor.title: Solution editor
SolutionEditor.placeholder: e.g. Write your solution to problem 3 — show your working and explain your steps.

DocumentEditor.help: A surface where the student uploads their own file(s); the tutor gives feedback on the active one. Composes with a checklist, note, etc.
DocumentEditor.title: Document upload
DocumentEditor.placeholder: e.g. Upload a photo of your handwritten solution to problem 3.

NoteEditor.help: A reference card shown in the workspace — instructions, a formula sheet, a definition. Supports Markdown.
NoteEditor.title: Note
NoteEditor.textPlaceholder:
e.g. **Speed:** v = s / t

Remember to convert to SI units.

WritingEditor.help: A box the student writes in — a conclusion, a reflection, a report section. They can download it as a file, and the tutor can read and comment on it. For hand-written physics working, use “Your solution” instead.
WritingEditor.title: Writing field
WritingEditor.taskPlaceholder: e.g. Write your conclusion — what do the measurements show, and why?
WritingEditor.wordTargetHelp: Shown to the student as a goal. It never blocks them from saving.

SimPicker.title: Simulation (optional)
SimPicker.none: No simulations available in this environment yet.
SimPicker.help: Host a vetted simulation in this activity — your lesson goal, checklist, and notes wrap it. The same sim can power many activities with different goals.

TableEditor.title: Data tables
TableEditor.help: A grid the student fills in (e.g. trial · time · velocity). Entered values are shared with the tutor so the student can ask about their own measurements.
TableEditor.noColumns: Add at least one column — a table with no columns won't be saved.
TableEditor.rows: Empty rows for the student to fill

ChartEditor.title: Charts
ChartEditor.help: Plots columns from the data table as the student fills it in (e.g. velocity against time). Add a data table with at least two number columns above so the chart has something to show.
ChartEditor.needTable: Add a data table with at least two number columns to choose axes.

CalculatorEditor.help1: • Name each variable with a short letter or word (e.g. m, c) — that's what you use in the formula.
CalculatorEditor.help2: • In the formula, write the right-hand side. Both E = m * c^2 and m * c^2 work — the result is shown for you.
CalculatorEditor.help4: • Allowed: + - * / ^ ( ) and sqrt, sin, cos, tan, ln, log, abs, exp.
CalculatorEditor.help5: • The student computes the result on their device, and what they get is shared with the tutor.
CalculatorEditor.intro: A formula the student computes — name the variables (e.g. m, c) and write the formula (e.g. E = m * c^2). The result is calculated on the student's device.
CalculatorEditor.title: Calculator
CalculatorEditor.nameRule: Variable names must start with a letter and contain no spaces — they're what you use in the formula.
CalculatorEditor.formulaHint: Write the right-hand side (the E = is optional). Put * between variables — m * c, not mc. Functions: sqrt, sin, cos, tan, ln, log, abs, exp.

ConceptMapEditor.help: The concepts this activity covers and what builds on what. Students see it as an orientation map; the tutor can run check questions per concept and light nodes up as they're demonstrated.
ConceptMapEditor.title: Concept map
ConceptMapEditor.doneWhenPlaceholder: Done when… — what counts as having got this concept
ConceptMapEditor.questionPlaceholder: Check question — the tutor asks this in the chat
ConceptMapEditor.answerPlaceholder: What a good answer covers (the tutor judges against this)

BuilderLayout.setupHint: Name it, choose the class, set the language.
BuilderLayout.lessonHint: What the tutor guides students to discover.
BuilderLayout.workspaceHint: Add a simulation and the tools students work with.
BuilderLayout.materialsHint: Curriculum the tutor can cite — optional.

ActivityBuilderBody.proposeConceptMap: Suggest a concept map for this activity: the key concepts, what builds on what, and when each concept counts as understood.
ActivityBuilderBody.name: Activity name
ActivityBuilderBody.languageHelp: The language students see this activity in, and the tutor replies in.
ActivityBuilderBody.goalPlaceholder: e.g. Guide students to discover why the horizontal and vertical components of projectile motion are independent — without giving the answer.
ActivityBuilderBody.goalHelp: This shapes how the tutor guides — it never gives the answer away. Write the goal, not the solution.
ActivityBuilderBody.workspaceIntro: Optionally host a vetted simulation — the same sim can power many activities with different goals — or keep it chat-only. Add a checklist, data table, chart, calculator, or note to structure the student's work.
ActivityBuilderBody.checklistHelp: Sub-steps students tick off as they work. Shown in the workspace; the tutor can see what's done.
ActivityBuilderBody.noChecklist: No checklist — the activity is an open conversation with the tutor. Add steps to give students a visible structure.

ActivityPreview.title: Preview — what students see
ActivityPreview.empty: Add elements (checklist, data table, chart, calculator or note) or a simulation to preview the students' workspace.
ActivityPreview.simAttached: {name} simulation attached. The live simulation appears here once the sandbox service is configured for this environment.

TemplatePicker.heading: Start from a template
TemplatePicker.hint: Click one to load it — the preview beside the builder shows what students will see. Everything stays editable.
TemplatePicker.blankSummary: A blank activity — write your own goal and add tools as you go.

MaterialsSection.teacherOnly: Curriculum library is teacher-only — sign in as a teacher.
MaterialsSection.loadFailed: Failed to load the curriculum library.
MaterialsSection.deleteFolderConfirm: Delete folder “{name}”? Its {count} document(s) will be unfiled, not deleted.
MaterialsSection.sharedWarning: This is in the SHARED library — every teacher using it will lose access.
MaterialsSection.ownWarning: This removes it from your library.
MaterialsSection.noAccess: You don't have access to this document.
MaterialsSection.libraryIntro: The shared document library. Upload documents, and file them by subject, folder and tag so they are findable when you build an activity. Every teacher sees — and can organise — the shared corpus.
MaterialsSection.citeIntro: Cite curriculum documents so the tutor can ground its answers with a source. Each cited document is either Reference — the tutor looks it up when relevant, right for a textbook — or In context, where the tutor is given the full text on every turn. Use In context for the task your students are working on, so the tutor never has to search for it or ask them to paste it in. Students only see the documents you mark visible.
MaterialsSection.stopContext: Stop always giving {label} to the tutor
MaterialsSection.contextTitle: The tutor always has this text — use it for the task students are working on. Costs prompt space on every turn.
MaterialsSection.referenceTitle: The tutor can look this up when relevant — the right choice for reference material.
MaterialsSection.subject: Subject
MaterialsSection.emptyLibrary: No documents yet. Browse the shared A/B/C library or upload your own.
MaterialsSection.unavailable: This document was added before content viewing existed — re-upload it to see what was extracted.
MaterialsSection.nothingExtracted: Nothing was extracted — check the file parsed correctly before relying on it.
MaterialsSection.truncated: Showing the first {shown, number} of {chars, number} characters.
MaterialsSection.saveFirst: Save the activity before adding an image.
MaterialsSection.share: Share to the shared library (asserts copyright clearance)

NewActivityPage.saveFailed: Could not create the activity — your changes were not saved. Please try again.
NewActivityPage.title: New activity
NewActivityPage.intro: Build a guided activity: set a teaching goal, add a workspace — a simulation, tables, a chart, a calculator, or guiding notes — and watch the live preview update as you go. Students join with a group code.
NewActivityPage.classesFailed: Could not load your classes. Refresh the page to try again.
NewActivityPage.noSkill: The activity tutor isn't set up here yet. Ask an administrator to add it, then you'll be able to create activities.
NewActivityPage.noClass: You don't have a class yet. <link>Create a class first</link> — an activity belongs to a class.
NewActivityPage.liveHelp: Students who join this class's group code can open it now and explore the topic you set. Configure it to add a workspace — a simulation, tables, a chart, a calculator, or guiding notes (and curriculum documents if you want).

ActivityConfigPage.saved: Saved — students see your teaching goal on their next turn
ActivityConfigPage.saveFailed: Save failed — your changes were not stored
ActivityConfigPage.loadFailed: Could not load this activity. Refresh to try again, or return to <link>Activities</link>.
ActivityConfigPage.title: Configure {name}
ActivityConfigPage.intro: You don't write system prompts here — write what you want students to get out of the activity. How the tutor teaches it comes from the tutor the class uses.
ActivityConfigPage.codeRoadmap: Planned for year two. You'll be able to build your own simulations with AI help, without writing code: describe what you want, preview it, and publish it once it has been checked. Each teacher keeps their own set. The aim is that your subject knowledge — not a developer's availability — decides what gets made.
ActivityConfigPage.check1: Safe — loads no scripts from outside
ActivityConfigPage.openQuestion: Open question for M/JB: review queue model (per-class trusted vs full institutional review)? Pedagogical-drift control — should research cohorts get a canonical pinned version?
ActivityConfigPage.noHistory: No history yet — save this activity to start its record.
ActivityConfigPage.adapted: Adapted from {source}’s activity. Your copy is independent — the original owner’s later edits don’t change it.
ActivityConfigPage.original: Created from scratch — this is an original activity.
ActivityConfigPage.historyRoadmap: A per-edit version timeline with one-click rollback is Year-2. The previous version would stay live for existing student sessions until they refresh.

ActivitiesPage.researchSubtitle: Every teacher's activities, in every state. Open one to see what they configured, or to edit it on their behalf.
ActivitiesPage.researchHint: All states (Draft / Private / Shared) across every teacher. Clicking opens the editor, which says whose activity it is.
ActivitiesPage.researchEmptyBody: No teacher has created an activity yet.
ActivitiesPage.deleteConfirm: Delete "{title}"? Students assigned to it will no longer see it.
ActivitiesPage.title: Activities
ActivitiesPage.statusHelp: Set each activity’s status with its chip — Private (your classes only) or Shared (other teachers can find and adopt a copy). Students only ever see activities you assign to their class.
ActivitiesPage.loadFailedBody: Something went wrong fetching the list. Try again in a moment.
ActivitiesPage.noMatchBody: Nothing in your library matches. Clear a filter, or try a different search.
ActivitiesPage.emptyBody: Create a from-scratch activity — a concept dialogue, a quiz, a lab notebook, or a sim — then assign it to one or more of your classes.
ActivitiesPage.sharedIntro: Published by other teachers. Use / adapt copies one into your library as a draft you can edit and assign.
ActivitiesPage.sharedNoMatch: No shared activities match these filters.
ActivitiesPage.adoptTitle: Copy into your library as a draft
ActivitiesPage.visibilityHelp: Draft = a new copy to review · Private = your classes only · Shared = other teachers can adopt a copy. Students only ever see activities you assign.
ActivitiesPage.draftNotice: Draft — not assignable yet. Review and save it to make it Private, then assign it to a class. Review & save

AuthoringCopilot.materialReference: · the tutor can look it up
